picks.t: Childish Gambino – The New World Tour (w/ WILLOW)
picks.d: Donald Glover brings his long-awaited return tour to Chase Center with WILLOW along for the ride — this one's been selling out everywhere. Expect a full theatrical production spanning his entire catalog, from 'Camp' to 'Because the Internet' and beyond. Grab your tickets now; this is the show everyone's going to be talking about next week.

The only citywide Hungry Ghost Festival in the entire nation — Portsmouth Square comes alive with art installations, music, and a jaw-dropping procession featuring a 14-foot Ghost King figure crafted by a traditional paper-craft master in Hong Kong. It's free, it's one night only, and it's genuinely unlike anything else happening in the country this weekend. Bring the whole crew.

Dev Hynes brings his impossibly lush blend of neo-soul, R&B, and art-pop to The Warfield for three consecutive nights — a rare residency format that lets him stretch out and get weird in the best way. Night 1 starts from $100, Night 2 from $87; both are worth every penny. If you only catch one night, go Wednesday for the opening-night energy.

picks.t: Weezer: The Gathering (w/ The Shins & Silversun Pickups)
picks.d: Three alt-rock legends on one stage at Chase Center — Weezer headlines with The Shins and Silversun Pickups in support, and yes, you will know every single word to every song. This tour follows their sold-out Blue Album 30th anniversary run, so expect the hits plus some surprises. A perfect mid-week treat-yourself moment.

picks.t: Liz Phair & Sleater-Kinney – The Flannel and The Fury 2026 (w/ Soccer Mommy)
picks.d: Three generations of indie rock women sharing one stage at the Greek Theatre Berkeley — Liz Phair, Sleater-Kinney, and Soccer Mommy in an outdoor hillside setting as summer winds down. The Greek is one of the most beautiful venues in the Bay Area and this lineup is genuinely historic. Doors at 5pm so get there early and soak it all in.

picks.t: Electroluxx Block Party: Purple Disco Machine & RuPaul
picks.d: A daytime outdoor block party at The Midway with Purple Disco Machine spinning house and disco heat alongside RuPaul — starting at $23, this is the best bang-for-your-buck party of the weekend. Festival vibes, drag spectacle, and enough bass to feel it in your chest. Show up in your best look.

The riot grrrl icons are back and they are still furious, still necessary, and still the loudest thing in any room they walk into. Formed in Olympia in 1990, Bikini Kill helped launch a feminist revolution in rock that's never really stopped reverberating. From $77 at The Warfield — a show you'll talk about for years.

SF's beloved monthly street party takes over 7th–12th Streets downtown with live music, performances, food, and pop-ups — and it's completely free. It's the perfect low-stakes first stop of the long Labor Day weekend before things get expensive fast. Grab a drink from a pop-up and just wander.

A string quartet battles it out between Queen and ABBA under flickering candlelight inside the stunning St. Ignatius Church — it's genuinely romantic and completely over-the-top in the best possible way. Tickets run $43–$100 and this is the kind of date night that writes itself. 'Bohemian Rhapsody' on strings hits different.

The San Francisco Symphony kicks off its 2026–27 season at Davies Symphony Hall with a month led by Giancarlo Guerrero, featuring Grammy-winners Samara Joy and Fantastic Negrito, Gregory Alan Isakov, and pianist Garrick Ohlsson. The season opener is always a special night — dressed up or dressed down, Davies Hall makes you feel like you're somewhere important. Check sfsymphony.org for tickets.

picks.t: Gothicumbia ft. Hot Goth GF, Los Ahijados de la Changa & Black Lipstick
picks.w: Fri Sep 4 · Doors 9 PM / Show 10 PM
picks.d: Gothic aesthetics meet cumbia rhythms in one of the most genuinely original late-night lineups you'll find in this city — at the Great American Music Hall, one of SF's most gorgeous historic rooms. LosGothsCo. throws a tight party and this one goes late. Wear black, dance hard.

picks.t: Free Outdoor Movie: Black Panther – Yerba Buena Gardens
picks.d: Grab a blanket and watch Black Panther on a big outdoor screen in the heart of SoMa — completely free with RSVP. Movie starts at sunset around 7:30 PM so stake out your spot early. Legendary film, fresh air, zero dollars out of pocket.

picks.t: Deep Purple & Jefferson Starship at Shoreline
picks.d: Two classic rock legends sharing a bill at Shoreline Amphitheatre as summer takes its last bow — Deep Purple's arena anthems paired with Jefferson Starship's Bay Area psychedelic legacy makes this a proper end-of-summer celebration. Shoreline is a great outdoor venue and this crowd is going to be having the time of their lives. Check Ticketmaster for seats.

ongoing.d: Free on Floor 1 — 75,000 hanging elements form a dreamlike canopy ceiling in the Roberts Family Gallery. Just walk in.
Five decades of the Mexican photographer's most powerful work, included with general admission through November 29.

ongoing.t: de Young Museum – 'A Gallery of Their Own'
ongoing.d: Four new galleries dedicated to Arts of Indigenous America; free for Bay Area residents every Saturday with ID.

ongoing.t: Asian Art Museum – 'Kim Minwook: On Carving, Bending and Binding Wood'
ongoing.d: Innovative woodworking installations running through March 2027 — free first Sundays.

ongoing.t: Asian Art Museum – 'FX Harsono: Writing in the Rain' (CLOSING Sep 7)
ongoing.d: Closes this Sunday — a video installation on memory and identity you don't want to miss.

ongoing.t: Hairspray at SF Playhouse (Final Week – Closes Sep 12)
ongoing.d: Eight Tony Awards, a joyful 1962 setting, and a soundtrack that won't leave your head. Last week to catch it.

ongoing.t: Whale's Tail Beer/Wine Garden – Golden Gate Park
ongoing.d: Free admission Saturdays with live music, food, drinks, and all the Golden Gate Park vibes you need.

ongoing.t: Volo Sports Coed Leagues – Sept Session
ongoing.d: Volleyball and pickleball leagues with built-in post-game bar hangs. Great way to meet people and get moving.
$10 drop-in races every weekend in Golden Gate Park and Lands End — the best $10 you'll spend all week.

new.name: Handroll Hawker
new.d: SF's first Australian-style sushi spot opening this September — get in before the lines form.

new.name: Sergeant Ma
new.d: From the team behind Trestle and Vault Steakhouse — Asian-inspired waterfront dining with serious pedigree.

new.name: Cinderella Bakery & Café Mission
new.d: Just landed on The Infatuation's SF Hit List — the newest must-visit for baked goods and café culture.

classic.name: Niku
classic.d: A5 wagyu, perfectly charred New York strips, and tomahawks the size of a child's head in a sleek-but-welcoming room.

classic.name: Sam Wo
classic.d: Over 100 years old and still going — BBQ pork noodle rolls and youtiao in SF's most historic dining room.

classic.name: Woods Beer & Wine Co. Pop-Up
classic.d: Their first-ever cocktail menu debuts at this Fisherman's Wharf pop-up — a great excuse to hit the waterfront.

bars.name: Iron Horse Cocktails
bars.d: Sleek SoMa spot hosting this week's singles speed dating game night — great drinks on any other night too.

bars.name: Blackbird
bars.d: A Castro institution with strong pours, a chill crowd, and the occasional themed event that gets weird in a good way.

bars.name: Vesuvio Café
bars.d: Beat-era North Beach institution next to City Lights Books — order a monk's ruin and feel smarter just sitting there.

bars.name: Zeitgeist
bars.d: Giant outdoor beer garden with 40+ taps, cash only, and the best people-watching in the Mission on a warm September night.

bars.name: El Techo
bars.d: Mission rooftop with city views, mezcal cocktails, and a vibe that makes every Tuesday feel like a Saturday.

bars.name: Brass Tacks
bars.d: Natural wines, warm lighting, and a Hayes Valley crowd that's effortlessly stylish — perfect post-symphony stop.

bars.name: Jonell's
bars.d: No frills, strong drinks, cheap prices, and somehow one of the friendliest rooms in the entire city.

bars.name: Harmonic Brewing
bars.d: Excellent IPAs, a laid-back taproom, and close enough to The Midway to make it your pre-show stop.

games.detail: Labor Day home opener — afternoon game at the ballpark, best hot dog in the Bay included in spirit.
Evening game under the lights at Oracle — grab garlic fries and a local IPA and remember why this ballpark is magic.
Wednesday matinee — the cheapest ticket in sports this week and a genuinely lovely way to spend a weekday afternoon.

sports.note: Tuesday's $15 seats are the sweet spot — great price, evening energy, and you can make it to Blood Orange at The Warfield after.
No home games this week — the Valkyries are on the road. Next home games: Sep 18 vs. Portland Fire (from $110) and Sep 19 vs. Seattle Storm (from $112). Mark your calendar!

concerts.t: Childish Gambino – The New World Tour (w/ WILLOW)
concerts.d: Donald Glover's long-awaited return tour lands at Chase Center with WILLOW as special guest. Expect a fully theatrical, emotionally heavy, visually stunning production spanning his entire catalog. Tickets from ~$44 but averaging ~$112 — move fast.

concerts.t: Weezer: The Gathering (w/ The Shins & Silversun Pickups)
concerts.d: Weezer headlines Chase Center with two of indie rock's most beloved supporting acts — The Shins and Silversun Pickups. Over 35 million records sold worldwide between these three bands. You will absolutely sing every word and feel no shame about it.

Three generations of essential indie rock women at the Greek Theatre Berkeley — one of the Bay Area's most gorgeous outdoor venues. Doors at 5pm, all ages welcome. This lineup is legitimately historic and the Greek hillside setting makes everything better.

Dev Hynes and his lush, deeply personal sound take up three nights at The Warfield. Wednesday from $100, Thursday from $87. A residency format means he can go deep into the catalog and experiment — these nights will feel intimate even in a room that holds 2,250.

The riot grrrl founders bring righteous punk fury to The Warfield for one night. Formed in Olympia in 1990, they ignited a feminist revolution in rock music that still resonates 35 years later. From $77 — one of the most historically significant shows of the month.

concerts.t: Electroluxx Block Party: Purple Disco Machine & RuPaul
concerts.d: Daytime outdoor block party at The Midway with two genuinely iconic names in house, disco, and drag culture. From $23 — this is the best deal of the weekend. Show up early, stay late, wear something fun.

concerts.t: Gothicumbia ft. Hot Goth GF, Los Ahijados de la Changa & Black Lipstick
concerts.d: Gothic energy meets cumbia rhythm in a late-night dance party at one of SF's most beautiful historic venues. LosGothsCo. puts on a tight, weird, genuinely fun show. Doors at 9pm — arrive close to 10 and the room will be at full energy.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check box office

concerts.d: A string quartet performs iconic hits from Queen and ABBA under flickering candlelight inside the beautiful St. Ignatius Church. It's romantic, theatrical, and completely over-the-top — in other words, perfect. Tickets $43–$100.

Giancarlo Guerrero leads the SF Symphony into a new season with a month of programming that includes Grammy-winners Samara Joy and Fantastic Negrito alongside Gregory Alan Isakov and pianist Garrick Ohlsson. The season opener at Davies is always a special evening — dressed up or not, the acoustics will hit you right in the chest.

A classic rock double-bill pairing Deep Purple's arena thunder with Jefferson Starship's Bay Area psychedelic legacy — at Shoreline as summer takes its final bow. Outdoor amphitheatre seating, warm September evening, and two bands who still absolutely deliver live.

concertsOngoing.t: Hairspray – SF Playhouse (Final Week, closes Sep 12)
concertsOngoing.d: Eight Tony Awards and one irresistible 1962 soundtrack — last chance this week before it closes Saturday.

concertsOngoing.t: Slayyyter – 'Wor$t Girl in the World Tour'
concertsOngoing.d: Tuesday Sep 8 at The Regency Ballroom, all ages — pop chaos with a cause, $1 per ticket goes to LGBTQI+ orgs.

concertsOngoing.t: World Arts West Dance Festival – Presidio Tunnel Tops
concertsOngoing.d: Free Sunday Sep 6, 1–4pm — live dance performances and workshops with some of the best views in the city.

singles.t: SF Singles Speed Dating Game Night
singles.d: Hosted by Fun Events at Iron Horse Cocktails, this one mixes speed dating rounds with actual icebreaker games so you're not just staring across a table making awkward small talk. Broken into age brackets so everyone in the room is actually in your zone. Low pressure, good drinks, and a Thursday night that might surprise you.

From $23, this daytime outdoor block party at The Midway with Purple Disco Machine and RuPaul is one of the best low-key ways to meet people this week — dancing in daylight removes approximately 90% of nightlife social anxiety. Easy to show up solo, easy to talk to strangers when the music is this good.

Free monthly street party from 7th to 12th Street downtown with live music, pop-ups, and food — the kind of casual, low-commitment evening that's genuinely easy to show up to solo. Five hours of programming means you can pop in for one drink and stay for four. No ticket, no plan required.

singles.t: DSE Runners Weekend Race – Golden Gate Park
singles.d: Ten dollars gets you into a weekend race with San Francisco's most social running club at Golden Gate Park or Lands End — post-run hangouts are half the point. Runners are notoriously friendly when they're also endorphin-flooded. The $10 drop-in is cash or PayPal at the start line.

singles.t: Volo Sports Coed Leagues – Sept Session
singles.d: Coed volleyball (6v6) at the JCC in Lower Pacific Heights and pickleball at The Crossing at East Cut — Volo builds in post-game bar meetups and social events so the socializing literally happens for you. Season runs ~$100–165/player and you meet people every single week for months. Arguably the best ROI in SF singles culture.

The Punch Line's legendary Sunday showcase features a rotating mix of established and emerging local comedians — intimate room, great crowd energy, and laughing together is genuinely one of the fastest ways to connect with someone new. From $10 and the SF Chronicle's pick for Best Comedy Club. Easy, fun, low-stakes Sunday night.

singlesOngoing.t: SF Mission Fun Runs / That Girl Run Club
singlesOngoing.d: Free weekly social runs through the Mission — friendly, low-key, and a genuinely great way to meet neighborhood people.
Comedy is one of the best date formats in the city — Cameron Esposito headlines Wednesday Sep 9 at 7:30pm from ~$45.

date.title: Candlelight & Chinatown Ghosts
date.tagline: Culture, history, and a little bit of the supernatural — all free.

steps.title: Castro Art Walk Opening
steps.detail: Start at the SF Railway Museum pop-up gallery for the Castro Art Walk opening — there's complimentary wine. Free art, free wine, great conversation starter.

steps.title: Chinatown Dinner
steps.detail: Walk to Chinatown and grab noodle rolls and youtiao at Sam Wo (one of SF's oldest restaurants). Casual, historic, and the story of the place is half the fun.

steps.title: Hungry Ghost Festival Procession
steps.detail: Head to Portsmouth Square for the Hungry Ghost Festival — the Ghost King procession is free, totally wild, and something neither of you has probably ever seen. Ends the night on a perfect note.

date.title: Candlelight & Late-Night Cumbia
date.tagline: Romance at St. Ignatius, then dancing until midnight at the GAMH.

steps.title: Pre-Show Drinks
steps.detail: Start at Brass Tacks in Hayes Valley for natural wines and good energy before the show. Keep it to one drink — the church has its own atmosphere.

steps.title: Candlelight: Queen vs. ABBA
steps.detail: Head to St. Ignatius Church for the string quartet concert. Flickering candles, soaring architecture, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' on violin. Tickets $43–$100 each — genuinely one of the most romantic things in the city this week.

steps.title: Gothicumbia at Great American Music Hall
steps.detail: Walk or Lyft to the Great American Music Hall. Doors at 9pm, show at 10pm — going from a candlelit church to a late-night cumbia dance party is an extremely good narrative arc for a first or second date.

date.title: Symphony Opener & Wagyu Dinner
date.tagline: Full elegance mode — season opener at Davies, then the best steak in SF.

steps.title: Niku for Dinner
steps.detail: Book Niku in the Design District early — A5 wagyu, tomahawks bigger than your head, and a room that makes you feel like a main character. Budget ~$150/pp.

steps.title: SF Symphony Season Opener
steps.detail: Head to Davies Symphony Hall for the 2026–27 season opener with Giancarlo Guerrero. The acoustics alone are worth the ticket price — check sfsymphony.org. Samara Joy is on the month's bill if you want to return.

steps.title: Nightcap at Brass Tacks
steps.detail: End the night in Hayes Valley with natural wine and the glow of a genuinely great evening. Low-key, warm, and close enough to walk to from Davies.

solo.title: Museum Day + Free Movie Night
solo.tagline: Art in the afternoon, Wakanda forever at sunset.

steps.title: SFMOMA – Giant Arc (Free)
steps.detail: Walk into SFMOMA's first floor and see Jacob Hashimoto's Giant Arc installation — 75,000 hanging elements covering the entire ceiling. Zero dollars, zero ticket required. Just walk in.

steps.title: Sam Wo Lunch in Chinatown
steps.detail: A 100-year-old Cantonese lunch counter with BBQ pork noodle rolls and youtiao. Eat at the counter, read the room, feel deeply SF. Under $15.

steps.title: Free Outdoor Movie: Black Panther
steps.detail: RSVP online (free) and bring a blanket to Yerba Buena Gardens. Sunset screening starts around 7:30pm. One of the best solo-friendly activities of the week — just show up and enjoy.

solo.title: Comedy Night + Late Nightcap
solo.tagline: Laugh hard, drink well, call it a perfect Thursday.

steps.title: Dinner at Zeitgeist
steps.detail: SF's beloved Mission beer garden with 40+ taps, cash only, and a laid-back crowd that's easy to talk to. Get a burger and a pint and sit outside in the September warmth.

steps.title: Cameron Esposito at Cobb's
steps.detail: Wednesday Sep 9 — Cobb's Comedy Club in North Beach for one of the sharpest comedians working today. From ~$45. The intimate 18+ room at Cobb's is perfect for solo attendance.

steps.title: Nightcap at Vesuvio
steps.detail: North Beach is right there — head to Vesuvio Café for a monk's ruin cocktail in the Beat-era bar next to City Lights Books. Sit at the bar, strike up a conversation, feel smarter than you did that morning.

solo.title: Blood Orange Night One + Dinner
solo.tagline: Solo at a residency night is an underrated power move.

steps.title: Dinner at Sergeant Ma
steps.detail: New Asian-inspired waterfront restaurant from the team behind Trestle and Vault Steakhouse — treat yourself to a proper solo dinner at one of September's most anticipated openings.

steps.title: Pre-Show at Harmonic Brewing
steps.detail: Head to Dogpatch and grab a pre-show IPA at Harmonic Brewing's taproom. Laid-back crowd, excellent beer, and it's close enough to The Warfield to Lyft easily.

steps.title: Blood Orange Night 1 at The Warfield
steps.detail: Dev Hynes opening a three-night residency at The Warfield — from $100. Going solo means you can completely lose yourself in the music without managing anyone else's experience. This is the one.

birthday.title: Ghost Festival Birthday Crew
birthday.tagline: Free, weird, memorable — exactly what birthdays should be.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Whale's Tail Garden
steps.detail: Start the celebration at the Whale's Tail beer garden in Golden Gate Park — free admission, live music, and a relaxed outdoor vibe to get everyone in the mood. Drinks for purchase but entry is free.

steps.title: Chinatown Dinner Crawl
steps.detail: March the crew to Chinatown for dinner at Sam Wo — order family style, tell everyone the wild history of the place, and make it an event. Cheap, delicious, deeply SF.

steps.title: Hungry Ghost Festival
steps.detail: End the night at Portsmouth Square for the Hungry Ghost Festival. The 14-foot Ghost King procession is free, totally unique, and the kind of shared experience that makes people talk about your birthday for years.

birthday.title: Weezer + Pre-Show Dinner
birthday.tagline: Collective nostalgia is the best birthday gift.

steps.title: Pre-Show Drinks & Appetizers
steps.detail: Gather the crew at El Techo rooftop bar in the Mission for mezcal cocktails and city views. The birthday person drinks first, obviously.

steps.title: Head to Chase Center
steps.detail: Doors open at 6pm for Weezer: The Gathering (Sep 9) — Silversun Pickups, The Shins, then Weezer. Budget ~$50–100/ticket. Everyone knowing every word to 'Undone' together is a genuine bonding experience.

steps.title: Post-Show at Harmonic Brewing
steps.detail: End at Harmonic Brewing in Dogpatch — laid back, great craft beer, and easy to keep the energy going without committing to a club. Best birthday move: let the birthday person pick the closing bar.

birthday.title: Childish Gambino Birthday Night
birthday.tagline: Go big. This show only comes around once.

steps.title: Niku Group Dinner
steps.detail: Book the big table at Niku in the Design District — A5 wagyu and massive tomahawks for the birthday crew. This is the kind of dinner that sets the tone for the whole night. Reserve well in advance.

steps.title: Childish Gambino at Chase Center
steps.detail: The New World Tour with WILLOW at Chase Center (Sep 8) — from ~$44 but budget higher for good seats. A full theatrical production for the birthday night. This is Donald Glover at peak artistry.

steps.title: Rooftop Nightcap
steps.detail: Close out at El Techo rooftop with the remaining crew — mezcal last call, city lights, and a recap of every moment from the night. The birthday person doesn't pay for anything all evening.

friends.title: First Thursdays + Ghost Festival Weekend
friends.tagline: Two free nights, zero planning, maximum stories.

steps.title: Downtown First Thursdays Block Party
steps.detail: Meet up at the First Thursdays block party downtown (7th–12th Streets) — free live music, pop-ups, food, and five hours of walking around with drinks. The perfect low-commitment group hang that somehow always turns into a great night.

steps.title: Divide and Conquer for Drinks
steps.detail: Let the group split up by vibe — dive bar crew heads to Jonell's, fancier crew heads to Brass Tacks. Regroup at midnight if you're feeling it.

steps.title: Hungry Ghost Festival
steps.detail: Reunite Saturday evening at Portsmouth Square for the Ghost Festival. Free, family-friendly until the procession starts, then genuinely eerie and wonderful. This is the 'you had to be there' moment of the week.

friends.title: Greek Theatre Girls Trip
friends.tagline: Liz Phair, Sleater-Kinney, Soccer Mommy — a literal dream lineup.

steps.title: Pre-Show Picnic at Tilden Park
steps.detail: Pack a picnic and head to the Berkeley hills before the show. Cheese, wine, snacks, and the kind of afternoon that feels like summer vacation. Doors at the Greek open at 5pm.

steps.title: Liz Phair & Sleater-Kinney at the Greek
steps.detail: Soccer Mommy opens, Sleater-Kinney plays, Liz Phair closes — at one of the most beautiful outdoor venues on the planet. All ages, hilltop setting, cool September evening. This is a lineup friends remember.

steps.title: Post-Show in Downtown Berkeley
steps.detail: End at a bar on Telegraph or Shattuck — Alchemy or Revival Brewing are easy post-show stops. Debrief every moment of the show over one more drink.

friends.title: Electroluxx + Late Dinner + Nightcap
friends.tagline: Day party energy into a full proper Saturday night.

steps.title: Electroluxx Block Party at The Midway
steps.detail: Purple Disco Machine and RuPaul from 3pm at The Midway — from $23/ticket, so you can afford to go all-in on the rest of the night. Dance in the afternoon sun and feel completely alive.

steps.title: Dinner at Sergeant Ma
steps.detail: Head to the new waterfront Asian-inspired restaurant from the Trestle team while you're still in a great mood from the block party. Group dinner, waterfront views, and a reservation you made smart.

steps.title: Late Night at Gothicumbia (GAMH)
steps.detail: Cap the night at the Great American Music Hall for Gothicumbia — show starts at 10pm. Going from a Purple Disco Machine block party to a gothic cumbia late-night is an extremely solid Saturday narrative.

parents.title: World Arts West + Free Movie Night
parents.tagline: Beautiful Sunday with the whole family, zero dollars.

steps.title: World Arts West Dance Festival – Presidio Tunnel Tops
steps.detail: Free Sunday Sep 6, 1–4pm at the Presidio with Tunnel Tops views of the Golden Gate Bridge. Live dance performances, interactive workshops, and the kind of outdoor setting that makes kids and adults equally happy.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Walk
steps.detail: Walk or drive into Golden Gate Park for the afternoon — the Whale's Tail Beer/Wine Garden has free admission and the kids can run around while you get a drink. Perfect transition between events.

steps.title: Free Outdoor Movie: Black Panther
steps.detail: Bring a blanket to Yerba Buena Gardens for the free outdoor screening of Black Panther (Sep 5) — movie starts at sunset around 7:30pm. Easy RSVP online, snacks encouraged, universally loved film.

parents.title: Giants Game + Chinatown Dinner
parents.tagline: A Labor Day classic — baseball, garlic fries, and Chinatown noodles.

steps.title: Giants vs. Cardinals – Labor Day Game
steps.detail: Monday Sep 7 afternoon game at Oracle Park — tickets from $40 for the holiday game. Garlic fries, local IPA, and nine innings of classic SF baseball. The ballpark is one of the best family experiences in the city.

steps.title: Chinatown Dinner at Sam Wo
steps.detail: Head to Chinatown after the game for dinner at Sam Wo — over 100 years old, BBQ pork noodle rolls, dumbwaiter still in use. Kids love the novelty, adults love the price and the history.

steps.title: Evening Stroll Through North Beach
steps.detail: Walk it off through North Beach — stop at City Lights bookstore (open late), peek into Vesuvio Café, and stroll Columbus Ave as the neighborhood comes alive. Zero cost, all atmosphere.

parents.title: de Young + Symphony Opening
parents.tagline: High culture Saturday — art in the park, symphony at night.

steps.title: de Young Museum (Free for Bay Area Residents)
steps.detail: Free Saturday admission with a Bay Area driver's license — reserve online. See 'A Gallery of Their Own,' the new Indigenous America galleries. The sculpture garden and the tower view are free for everyone.

steps.title: Japanese Tea Garden & Park Picnic
steps.detail: Pack a lunch or grab something from a park vendor and eat in Golden Gate Park near the Japanese Tea Garden (tickets ~$12–15/adult, free under 5). Relaxed, beautiful, genuinely restorative.

steps.title: SF Symphony Season Opener
steps.detail: End the day at Davies Symphony Hall for the 2026–27 season opener (Tue Sep 8) — or plan accordingly for the right evening. Giancarlo Guerrero conducts with Samara Joy and Fantastic Negrito in the month's programming. Check sfsymphony.org for family pricing.
